case.presentation: Patient is a 35-year old woman who had unprotected vaginal intercourse with a male partner who has recently been diagnosed with HIV. The patient is requesting PEP despite being outside of the 72-hour window. What testing should be ordered for this patient and is PEP indicated?
case.recommendations: The appropriate testing to order is (HIV antigen/Ab and HIV RNA), along with hepatitis B panel (HBsAg, HBsAb, HBcAb), hepatitis C antibody, syphilis serology (RPR or treponemal test), and NAAT for gonorrhea and chlamydia with site-specific sampling based on sexual practices. Testing can be done at 2 weeks, 1 month, and 3 months post-exposure or any time the patient has symptoms of acute HIV infection. No PEP indicated at this time given patient is outside the 72-hour window. Counsel the patient to use condoms or abstain from sexual intercourse until final HIV testing confirms a negative status, discuss other STIs that may have been acquired during the exposure and offer appropriate testing, and educate her about pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for future HIV risk reduction if ongoing exposure risk exists.
